answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring every identity to complete a staking voyage before it may attest: each agent bonds capital that is slashed whenever peers it vouched for diverge or fail. Because every fresh identity starts from that same deposit, running a thousand fake agents multiplies the collateral an attacker must lock, not his reward. Reaching the summit of the reputation graph earns nothing permanent, and reputation is not a private island—it decays continuously, so abandoned colluding nodes fall out of the quorum unless the attacker keeps paying to sustain them.
